metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Malta

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Malta using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically provides sampling weights (and, where applicable, replicate weights) to support population-representative estimation and correct uncertainty quantification. The factsheet itself does not specify which weight variable(s) (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate-weight method were applied in the displayed estimates, so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For analysts reproducing these estimates from microdata, the recommended approach is to use the official PISA 2022 weights and replicate weights supplied with the database and to follow the PISA Reader’s Guide/technical documentation for variance estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related associations; it does not provide an analysis section describing how plausible values (PV-based achievement scores) were generated/combined or how missing data were handled in an empirical modeling pipeline. The reported outcomes are presented as OECD estimates (means, proficiency shares, relative differences, and variance explained) rather than as results from a user-specified ML model with documented PV and missing-data procedures. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling details are not available in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for methodological replication.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Malta’s PISA 2022 creative thinking results for 15-year-old students. It states that, in Malta, 3,127 students in 46 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 4,000 15-year-olds (estimated 93% of the total population of 15-year-olds). The text does not describe additional analytic exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items, specific creative-thinking task completion rules), so the analytic sample is treated as the available PISA sample for Malta used by OECD to produce the published estimates.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for Malta among 15-year-old students. Creative thinking is assessed with 32 open-ended tasks scored by human judgement using rubrics, covering three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Malta’s mean creative thinking score is 31 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33). Malta also shows a relative pattern: creative thinking is above what would be expected from mathematics and reading performance, with 41% of the variation in creative thinking uniquely attributed to mathematics performance (correlations of 0.73 with both mathematics and reading). The factsheet further reports within-Malta gaps by socioeconomic status (advantaged students outperform disadvantaged by 10.1 points) and gender (girls outperform boys by 4.6 points), plus associations between creative-thinking-related beliefs/attitudes and performance. Because this is a descriptive OECD factsheet rather than an ML study, no predictive model metrics or algorithmic methods are reported here.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet that reports descriptive international comparisons and selected associations, not an original empirical ML study with a specified predictive pipeline. As a result, fields such as ML techniques, target-variable-specific predictive findings, and documented PV/missing-data handling for a modeling procedure are not applicable from the provided text. The extraction therefore focuses on the assessment design and the reported performance benchmarks and gaps for Malta.
